added_failures_note: The reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite JSON, so no paired suite arm exists to diff. The completed head arm in review-named-gate.log ran at revision b5b31671c7d7b3712fa0dc4b316b76be6d2a669c, whose imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py and tests/test_telemetry_index.py are byte-identical to reviewed head 5ef2f874, and reports 97 passed with EXIT=0 and no failing test ids, so the added-failure set is empty. The only failing arm recorded in the run is named-tests.log at db9343d1+working (95 passed, 1 failed: tests/test_telemetry_ingest.py::test_a_tick_opens_no_source_unchanged_since_the_last_tick), which the manifest lists under retry_failures and which passes at the head gate; that file is outside the node's write paths, so it was not the node's to repair.
call_sites: imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:3383 TelemetryIndex(resolved_index) in the ingest command

findings.text: follow-on: `assert digested == []` can no longer fail. The monkeypatch one line above at tests/test_telemetry_index.py:2054 replaces telemetry_index._digest_of, but after this change the full-prefix read on a changed source goes through _hash_of (imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:1943), which _digest_of merely wraps and which the patch does not intercept, so counting_digest is never called and digested is always empty whatever the pass reads. The property survives only through `assert opened == []` at tests/test_telemetry_index.py:2058, which patches Path.open and does catch both a re-probe and a re-digest, so the assertion itself now reports coverage it does not provide.

follow-on: `_digest_of` has no production caller after this change. Its only caller was the comparison inside `_was_rewritten`, replaced here by `_hash_of` (imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:1943), so the helper is now dead production code kept alive solely by the monkeypatch at tests/test_telemetry_index.py:2054 that no longer intercepts anything. Delete it with the stale hook, or keep it as the named owner of the digest capability, but leaving it referenced only by a no-op patch makes the read path's digest story unreadable.

follow-on: `_tier_has_no_row` now declines to scan the file on any recorded source row, while its docstring at imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:1383 still justifies the shortcut by 'A file already consumed whole carried rows when it was read'. The condition is strictly broader than the documented one: a partially consumed row, or a row left by an inode reused for a different file, also short-circuits the _holds_a_record_line scan. The behaviour is the conservative direction (the tier is offered and read), so this is a documentation defect rather than a live one, but a reader deciding what the guard covers is misled by the narrower claim.
